title: Select dielectric data for the actual laminate construction
summary: Use construction- and frequency-specific dielectric data. FR-4 is not one fixed permittivity; Isola tables distinguish reinforcement, resin content and thickness.
applies_to: PCB engineering review; apply the stated model and source scope.
required_inputs: Fabricator material and construction; frequency; applicable Dk data
verification: Confirm the construction used by the impedance model.
limitations: FR408HR values do not characterize every FR-4 board; published nominal data are not fabrication tolerances.

citations.locator: Revision D, page 1, Core Data table

title: Separate dielectric loss from impedance targeting
summary: Record dissipation factor separately from dielectric constant and retain its frequency and construction. Meeting an impedance target does not by itself establish acceptable channel loss.
applies_to: PCB engineering review; apply the stated model and source scope.
required_inputs: Channel bandwidth and applicable Dk/Df data
verification: Review loss against the selected interface budget.
limitations: A material table alone does not model connector, conductor and via losses.

title: Use a bounded microstrip estimate with explicit units
summary: For the source surface-microstrip approximation: Z0 = 87/sqrt(er+1.41) * ln(5.98*h/(0.8*w+t)). Use consistent length units for h, w and t; er is dimensionless and Z0 is ohms.
applies_to: PCB engineering review; apply the stated model and source scope.
required_inputs: Target impedance, reference spacing h, width w, finished copper t, relative permittivity er
verification: Identify this approximate model; validate geometry with the fabrication solver.
limitations: TI discusses best accuracy around 50-100 ohms. This is not a coupled-pair, coplanar or soldermask-aware solver; source examples are not guaranteed widths.

citations.locator: Appendix B, section 13.2.1, Figures 47-48 and following example, pages 117-118

title: Keep impedance, heating and voltage-drop calculations separate
summary: Record the calculator version, model, input units and assumptions. Use a transmission-line model for impedance and an electrical/thermal model for power conductors; review via behavior separately.
applies_to: PCB engineering review; apply the stated model and source scope.
required_inputs: Routing structure; copper and environment; current and allowable rise; applicable model
verification: Check geometry, heating and drop against their own requirements.
limitations: KiCad 9 documentation describes IPC-2221 track-width estimates. Check the installed version; those estimates are not measured thermal qualification or IPC-2152 certification.

citations.locator: TransLine, Via Size and Track Width sections; retain source edition

title: Review system ground loops without cutting signal references
summary: Map ground connections through supplies, cables and interconnected boards before diagnosing unwanted loop currents. A proposed star connection can acquire additional paths through other equipment.
applies_to: PCB engineering review; apply the stated model and source scope.
required_inputs: Full system connections and sensitive reference nodes
verification: Trace possible return paths across the assembled system.
limitations: Do not treat all multiple ground connections as faults or split a plane automatically. This guidance does not authorize altering protective-earth or isolation provisions.

citations.locator: Pages 11-14, multicard grounding and mixed-signal devices

title: Check noise caused by shared return impedance
summary: A load current sharing impedance with a sensitive reference can create an error voltage. Review the current path and connection impedance, rather than assuming every GND-labelled point has identical potential.
applies_to: PCB engineering review; apply the stated model and source scope.
required_inputs: Aggressor current and sensitive measurement return
verification: Inspect shared return segments and measure reference disturbance under load.
limitations: This mechanism is distinct from merely spotting a geometric loop. Follow the converter-specific grounding requirements.
